title: Find what axe can't
prompt: This part of Ticketly passes an axe scan with **zero violations**. A screen reader user still runs into four real WCAG failures. Select the lines a human reviewer would flag. (`.section-title` is styled to look exactly like the other section headings, and `addToBasket()` writes "Ticket added" into `#basket-status`.)
hints: axe checks that things exist. Look for things that exist but mean the wrong thing.
Compare what a sighted user sees with what the accessibility tree says, line by line.
One problem is about text, one about structure, one about dynamic updates, and one about voice control.
explanation:
**Line 3:** `alt="image"` is present, so axe is satisfied, but it tells a screen reader user nothing ("image, image"). Describe the photo or, if it is decorative, use `alt=""`. **Line 4:** the paragraph looks like a section heading but isn't one, so it is missing from heading navigation (1.3.1 Info and Relationships). Use `

Tickets

`. **Line 8:** `#basket-status` changes after each click, but it isn't a live region, so screen readers announce nothing (4.1.3 Status Messages). Add `role="status"`. **Line 9:** the visible text is "Reserve seats" but the accessible name is "Book", so a voice control user saying "click Reserve seats" gets nothing (2.5.3 Label in Name). Remove the `aria-label`. axe has a rule for this, but it is experimental and off by default. The other lines are fine: the input is labelled, the buttons and link have clear names.
